summary.headline: Elgi Q1 FY27 revenue grew about 23% (7 points from exchange), EBITDA up 28%, with EBITDA margin held flat year on year at prior-year level.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue growth of about 23%, of which about 7 points were exchange-related, with growth across all geographies. EBITDA grew about 28% and EBITDA margin was maintained at last year's level despite raw material inflation, tariffs and adverse product mix. PAT margin was about 9.7%, roughly flat YoY, after exceptional reorganisation costs in Australia, Europe and the US. Management said price corrections to offset metal cost inflation would take effect towards the end of Q2 and more fully in Q3, so the Q1 margin does not yet reflect them.

financial_highlights.value: Maintained at prior-year level, management said slightly better
Up about 12%, mainly rental premises for motor plant and US facilities sold and leased back
About 1.6-1.8 million of approx. 4 million approved; balance pending

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Grew about 28%, described as primarily volume-driven, with growth across industrial, portables, aftermarket and vacuum. Growth cited in EV ecosystem, renewables and semiconductor supply chains; water well segment picked up in the quarter.

segments.name: North America
segments.commentary: Grew about 37%. Distribution business underperformed, mainly on service side; other businesses performed well.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Grew about 21%. Run as a P&L play now, targeted at breakeven; plans to enter Germany and expand in Eastern Europe, with tighter cost control.

segments.name: Australia
segments.commentary: Grew about 17% but described as muted; service and distribution operations being reset, with recovery expected by Q3-Q4.

segments.name: Southeast Asia
segments.commentary: Described as a challenge for an Indian brand; not a significant contributor; longer-term play.

segments.name: Vacuum (Italian JV product)
segments.commentary: Locally produced and selling since indigenisation; management described Q1 growth as phenomenal in percentage terms from a small base, with no figure given.

guidance_outlook: Price corrections to recover raw material inflation expected to kick in towards end of Q2 FY27 and fully in Q3 FY27; management said Q1 under-recovered on raw material costs of 5-6% versus 3-4% planned.
Management expects EBITDA margin to keep improving, citing operating leverage, product launches, constant cost reduction and fixed cost rationalisation over 3-4 years.
Medium-term EBITDA margin target of 20%; prior guidance of 18% by 2031 was mentioned in Q&A.
Tier 4 entry-level compressor range to launch formally in September 2026 (Hyderabad exhibition); first orders already received; marginal contribution to top line this year.
Demand=Match to be introduced in rest-of-world models during 2026; management expects all products to carry it within about a year.
Some reorganisation costs in Australia, Europe and the US expected to continue into the year.
capex_capacity: Capex mainly for MK2, the programme to shift the campus from the city factory to a new campus; about half of capex.
Land purchased in Italy under a commitment made six years earlier, plus routine factory equipment.
Motor plant moved to rented premises; US facilities sold and replaced with rental facilities.
Insourced motor manufacturing cited as a significant cost-saving driver.
demand_pricing: Inquiry levels described as very strong, though deal finalisation timelines are longer than normal.
Price correction only marginal in Q1; growth described as primarily volume-driven.
Demand=Match technology, launched September 2025, is embedded in tier 1-3 models as standard and cited as a key driver of new-customer wins in India.
Aftermarket parts are about 28-30% of India revenue and about 15-16% globally (parts only); management said global service benchmark is about 38%.
Warranty cost stated as below 1% of revenue; management said competitors are higher, though not publicly reported.
Steel sector capacity utilisation weak; management said steel is bleeding capacity utilisation before new investment.

qa_highlights.question: How much of India's 28% growth was volume versus price?
qa_highlights.answer: Primarily volume-driven, with only a marginal price correction in Q1; raw material costs rose 5-6% versus the 3% planned, and management expects to recover this in later quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is Elgi gaining Indian market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it thinks so but would prefer competitors confirm it.

qa_highlights.question: What is the aftermarket share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Parts are about 20-23% of group revenue, about 28-30% in India and about 15-16% in the rest of the world; service is a small part in India and is left largely to dealers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the warranty cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Less than 1% of revenue; competitors are believed to be higher than 1%, though not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What drove margin improvement in international subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: North America growth, restructuring to lean the organisation, cost reduction including in-house motor manufacturing, and price holding in Q1, with price corrections expected to add from Q2-Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will employee and operating costs rationalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost ratios should fall as revenue grows; a process-layer project over 3-4 years is expected to identify lower-cost locations for specific jobs.

risks_watch: Tariffs at 25%; outstanding tariff refund balance (approx. 4 million approved, 1.6-1.8 million received) and future US tariff policy.
Raw material inflation: management said price corrections lag cost inflation, so Q2 margins could be pressured before recovery.
Australia service and distribution reset and Southeast Asia challenges.
Reorganisation costs expected to continue into the year, which may keep PAT margin under pressure.
Distribution build-out in the US and globally is slow; management said adding distributors takes a long time.
Tier 4 launch in a segment where low-cost Chinese compressors compete on price.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, margins and product technology, but cautious on near-term price recovery timing and on Australia, Southeast Asia and US distribution. Management declined to give several figures (segment mix, semiconductor share, warranty cost, vacuum sales).
key_quotes: We grew by about 23% and after that 7% was exchange related.
So even this quarter, we have maintained our EBITDA percentage same as last year.
Demand=Match is a technology that gets embedded in all our products, right?
So, we are confident that there will not be any impact.
